prompt: How many controls do the CIS Controls v8 and v8.1 have?
Why does inventory come first in the CIS Controls?

choices.text: Because it is alphabetical
choices.why: The list is in priority order.

choices.text: Because it is the cheapest control to buy
choices.why: Cost is not the reason for the order.

choices.text: Because auditors check it first
choices.why: The order follows how a defence is built, not audits.

choices.text: Everything else depends on it
choices.why: Right. Nobody patches a server nobody remembers.

prompt: Match each lesson to the CIS Control it serves.
What do the CIS Controls give a small team that ISO 27001 and the NIST CSF do not?
hint: The question a small team actually has.

choices.text: A certificate to show customers
choices.why: The CIS Controls are not certifiable.

choices.text: A legal requirement to comply with
choices.why: They are voluntary.

choices.text: A complete list of every possible control
choices.why: They are a short list on purpose.

choices.text: Where to start
choices.why: Right. A prioritised order.

prompt: Match each implementation group to its cumulative number of safeguards.
Which implementation group fits the shop, and why?

choices.text: IG2, because it sells online
choices.why: Selling online does not by itself move it up.

choices.text: None, since it is too small
choices.why: IG1 is meant for every organisation.

choices.text: IG1: one IT person and ordinary data
choices.why: Right. Essential cyber hygiene.

choices.text: IG3, because every business should aim for the top
choices.why: Groups describe needs, not ambition.

prompt: An IG1 organisation does all 56 safeguards well; an IG3 one claims all 153 and does half. Which is better placed?

choices.text: They are equal, since both are certified
choices.why: The CIS Controls do not certify.

choices.text: The IG3 one, since it covers more
choices.why: Claimed is not done.

choices.text: The IG1 one
choices.why: Right. What is done well counts.

choices.text: Neither; only IG2 is meaningful
choices.why: Every group is meaningful for its organisations.

choices.text: The list of 18 CIS Controls
choices.why: That is a different publication.

choices.text: A certificate for secure products
choices.why: Benchmarks certify nothing.

choices.text: A configuration guide for one product
choices.why: Right. Setting, rationale, audit, remediation, impact.

choices.text: A speed test for servers
choices.why: The word benchmark misleads here.

prompt: What is the difference between Level 1 and Level 2 in a benchmark?

choices.text: Level 2 costs money, Level 1 is free
choices.why: Cost is not what separates them.

choices.text: Level 1 is for Windows, Level 2 for Linux
choices.why: Each benchmark has both levels.

choices.text: Level 2 is stricter and breaks more
choices.why: Right. Chosen item by item where risk justifies it.

choices.text: Level 1 is optional, Level 2 is required
choices.why: Level 1 is the baseline everybody starts from.

prompt: Why does a freshly installed server need a checklist at all?
hint: Defaults have to work for everyone.

choices.text: Servers forget their settings after a week
choices.why: Drift comes from changes, not forgetting.

choices.text: Vendors ship insecure software on purpose
choices.why: Defaults favour compatibility, not malice.

choices.text: Installation always fails silently
choices.why: It works; it is just permissive.

choices.text: They favour convenience, not security
choices.why: Right. A configuration vulnerability with no bug.

prompt: The file showed #PermitRootLogin prohibit-password. Why did the lesson not trust it?

choices.text: Because root can never log in over SSH
choices.why: Root could log in with a key, as sshd -T showed.

choices.text: The file is not the configuration
choices.why: Right. Ask the program with sshd -T.

choices.text: grep shows only the first line of a file
choices.why: It showed every matching line.

choices.text: The file was encrypted
choices.why: It was read in plain text.

prompt: Before the fix, how many of the four checklist lines failed?
After the fix, the main file still says X11Forwarding yes on line 99, and the check passes. Why?

choices.text: X11 forwarding cannot be turned on in a lab
choices.why: It was on before the fix.

choices.text: sshd -t removed line 99
choices.why: sshd -t only checks validity.

choices.text: The first value read wins
choices.why: Right. Exactly why reading the file misleads.

choices.text: Line 99 is ignored because it is too far down
choices.why: Distance is not the rule.

prompt: Why did ana put the four settings in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-shop.conf rather than editing the main file?

choices.text: The main file is read-only on Ubuntu
choices.why: It can be edited; there is a better place.

choices.text: Because sshd ignores the main file
choices.why: It reads it; the included file comes first.

choices.text: To hide the settings from auditors
choices.why: Nothing is hidden; sshd -T shows the result.

choices.text: So a package update does not undo them
choices.why: Right. The shop's settings live in the shop's file.

prompt: The checklist reports four PASS lines. What does that mean?

choices.text: The server is secure
choices.why: It means the known items are right.

choices.text: Only that the known items are right
choices.why: Right. It says nothing about who holds the keys.

choices.text: The server passed its ISO 27001 audit
choices.why: A checklist is not an audit.

choices.text: Nobody can log in to the server
choices.why: Keys still work.

prompt: A partner cannot use SSH keys, so one server must accept passwords. What does the lesson say to do with that checklist line?

choices.text: Delete the line from the checklist
choices.why: That hides the decision.

choices.text: Switch the checklist off for that server
choices.why: The other items still matter there.

choices.text: A dated, accepted exception
choices.why: Right. With a compensating control where one exists.

choices.text: Leave it failing; everyone will understand
choices.why: Permanent failures teach people to ignore failures.

prompt: A server changing away from its checked settings over time is called configuration ___.
